curated-gf-euphoria-script-fs-hoover: Loose, looping pen letters up top. Hoover, a text serif, gives them a sturdy footing, say, for a family recipe keepsake, and it stays comfortable to read in short bursts.
curated-gf-festive-gf-rosario: Festive looks brushed on, its letters nearly touching. Rosario sits beside it open and modern, so the shrunken lowercase of one meets the friendlier, more generous shapes of the other.
curated-gf-finger-paint-gf-mochiy-pop-on: Chunky, tall-bodied letters with barely a size step. Mochiy Pop One, a sans with huge lowercase eyes and one stroke width, feels like a mild, tidy neighbor to that loud heading.
curated-gf-finger-paint-gf-suez-one: Suez One brings a bookish, open-eyed serif texture. Finger Paint is the one that commands attention with tall, thick-stroked bodies, while the body font does its best work in short stretches of reading.
curated-gf-fleur-de-leah-gf-kosugi: Friendly, swelling script up front. Kosugi follows as a plain sans with a wire-bent look, so a workshop class sign up, say, would read smoothly once the text runs on.
curated-gf-fleur-de-leah-gf-noto-serif-s: Brushy swells and hairline tapers, loose as handwriting. Noto Serif SC meets that with a literary serif whose strokes thicken gently, which makes the closed and open letterforms the pair's best trick.
curated-gf-fleur-de-leah-gf-overpass-mon: Casual, swelling strokes lead here. Overpass Mono follows in fixed-width, uniform letters (handy for a dj night flyer), and that stiff monospace rhythm gives the script something to push against.
curated-gf-flow-block-fs-rowan: Flow Block is buttoned up, with a compact middle band and rope-like strokes, something a leatherwork stamp might use. Rowan, a classic serif, opens up every curve and lets thin strokes sit lightly against the thick.
curated-gf-flow-block-gf-aoboshi-one: Aoboshi One is a traditional serif with shrunken lowercase and no thin-to-thick shifts. Flow Block handles expressive display work, like a soda shop ice cream sign, while Aoboshi One is better kept to brief text.
curated-gf-flow-rounded-gf-kay-pho-du: Pursed, constant-width rounded letters set the tone, maybe for a coffee roaster for outdoorsy types. Kay Pho Du follows with open, reed-like counters, and a text serif like that keeps reading easy in short stretches.
